title: Tiger Road MD: day one
summary: Starting a Mega Drive port of Capcom's Tiger Road by running the arcade's own 68000 code on the console.
cover_alt: Tiger Road on the Mega Drive: the hero swings an axe in a pink-walled hall beside a giant stone statue wrapped in snakes, while soldiers attack.

title: Tiger Road NG: day one
summary: A second Tiger Road port, this time to the Neo Geo: the same arcade code, with backgrounds rebuilt from sprites and the music adapted to a different sound chip.
cover_alt: Tiger Road on the Neo Geo: the PRESS START screen, with the hero and an ogre-like enemy in a ruined stone room.

title: Cruis'n USA DC: the arcade, not the N64
summary: Bringing the original arcade Cruis'n USA to the Dreamcast, starting from the arcade code rather than the Nintendo 64 version, and finding out the hardware gap is wider than I thought.
cover_alt: Cruis'n USA on the Dreamcast: a silver car approaches the Golden Gate Bridge past road barriers, palm trees and a cypress.

title: Shadow Warrior DC: the console version it never had
summary: A fan port of 3D Realms' 1997 Build engine shooter to the Dreamcast, starting from the released source code and its portable JFShadowWarrior version.
cover_alt: Shadow Warrior on the Dreamcast: the red title menu with New Game, Load Game, Save Game, Options and Credits over a yin-yang symbol.

title: Cruis'n USA DC: progress report
summary: A few weeks into the Dreamcast port of the arcade Cruis'n USA: how the V-Unit code gets onto the console, the problems solved along the way, the extras, and where performance stands.
cover_alt: Cruis'n USA on the Dreamcast: a red sports car drives off-road past tree stumps towards a redwood forest, in 10th place.

title: Shadow Warrior DC: two weeks in
summary: Two weeks of Shadow Warrior on the Dreamcast: fewer pauses for disc reads, saves that fit on a VMU, music that picks up where it left off, VGA output and a hand-drawn logo on the VMU.
cover_alt: Shadow Warrior on the Dreamcast: Lo Wang holds a katana on a wooden boat crossing water between rock walls, a medkit at his feet.

title: Cruis'n USA DC: Arcade Edition
summary: Almost there: the arcade Cruis'n USA running natively on the Dreamcast, now at full arcade speed on real hardware. Here's what it adds over the original.
cover_alt: Cruis'n USA on the Dreamcast: a bronze 1960s sports car kicks up dust on the grassy verge of the LA freeway, past palm trees and a hillside house.

title: Shadow Warrior DC: 30th Anniversary Edition
summary: The Dreamcast port of Shadow Warrior becomes the 30th Anniversary Edition: both official expansions built in, a new start-up screen, fewer disc reads during play and a new Performance Mode.
cover_alt: Shadow Warrior on the Dreamcast: Lo Wang holds a minigun in a wooden building as a Flash Bomb pickup message appears on screen.

title: Karnov MD: the simpler one?
summary: Partly because it looked easier to adapt than Tiger Road, partly because an unofficial Neo Geo version exists, a few days ago I started porting Data East's Karnov to the Mega Drive. Here's where it stands.
cover_alt: Karnov on the Mega Drive: Karnov stands among stone ruins between two tall buildings, with the item bar at the top of the screen.

title: Tiger Road MD: two weeks of polish
summary: Two weeks after the first post, the Mega Drive port of Tiger Road has steadier colours, fewer flickering sprites, better sound on real hardware and a proper attract mode.
cover_alt: Tiger Road on the Mega Drive: the hero rides a horse through a dark forest at night, with a stormy sky and distant mountains.

title: Tiger Road MD: three languages and stereo
summary: The Mega Drive port of Tiger Road now speaks Japanese, corrected English and Spanish, plays its music in stereo, and makes a few cuts where the console can't keep up with the arcade.
cover_alt: Tiger Road on the Mega Drive: the hero, with an axe, faces two giant green-armoured twin bosses in front of painted warrior portraits.
